assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_TOKUDA_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (17,951 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false), a portrait of Tokuda Kazuhiko (Toku-san) in Asaura's Japanese Ordinary days: the pitch (S9), the assignment and Mika's limit (S13), the group reference shoot (S15), the work session and Kana's spoon (S17), the talk about Kana (S18), the delivery of the issue (S19) and the bonus feature shoot (S22), located by spine item and paragraph. Its closing section states his most strongly supported impulse in a variation and what remains untested. The discovery row claims behavior, psychology, relationships and decision-making, and does not claim speech or ethics. He has no television identity and does not appear in Recovery days. The sequential readings, crosswalk and readiness record the portrait links are not curated on this subject; no claim rests on them, and the readiness record was read only as calibration input. The project's COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY outcome was not adopted as a grade. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Ordinary days only. His history belongs to him at every state, so far as the portrait gives it: twenty-eight, divorced, no children, a freelance magazine writer; the student who hunted obscure films in rental stores (9.2-23, 15.63-79). Located states: a regular greeted with his usual since about the previous week, the pitch and Mika's refusal (9.12-189); the ten-page assignment and Mika's turned-aside question (13.2-49); the takoyaki (13.37-72); the group reference shoot (15.2-105); the work session and Kana's spoon (17.2-91); the talk about Kana's journeys (18.32-64); the feature shoot, printed after the signed afterword but occurring before the delivery (22.2-56); the delivery of the issue and his changed priority (19.7-78). The split falls at 19.49-78: before it his wish to be the one who introduces the café is foremost; after it the café's being special to him matters more, with the wish dwindled but not gone. His later career is outside the evidence.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The portrait gives a located account: a wish to be first to discover and introduce, traced to his student film hunting and recognized in the café pitch (9.113-125, 15.63-79); pleasure in being recognized as a regular (9.12-37); an observer who notices a break in the room's behavior and then talks himself out of a secret (9.62-112, 9.137-149); readiness to stop when Mika turns a question aside (13.13-23, 13.45-49); pride in his copy and hurt when it is passed over (19.28-70); a priority that shifts from being special to the café to the café being special to him (19.49-78). It predicts his mistakes: overconfidence before the shoot (15.30-56), treating his idea of emancipation as Mizuki's (9.73-93), explanations of others' skill built from appearance (15.63-105), and a benign account of Kana (18.32-64). Not B: the portrait's own forecast for a sensitive anecdote offers alternatives (one careful question, welcoming a lead, remembering without attribution), and his response when a subject objects to publication is untested, so whether attachment or the wish to publish decides such a choice is open, which is insufficiency (22.46-56, 19.44-65). Not D: a dedicated portrait locates conditions for his conduct as regular, observer and feature writer.

Ordered states across Ordinary days with a named change: from the pitch to the delivery the wish to introduce the café dwindles, and the narrator catches him correcting himself (9.113-125, 19.49-78). Not B: one change within one book, with sparse intervals. Not D: the states and their triggers are located.

The row does not claim speech and the portrait does not analyze it. Located only as reported speech acts: telling Mika the question is personal (13.13-23), saying he will of course come back (9.161-189), asking what happened and saying the issue is for the people involved (19.7-49); いつもの is Mika's word, not his. Not D: no register is described.

Located habits: the center counter seat and usual light-roast American (9.12-37); laptop work in a café he likes, rationalized and overrun, with sugar tipped into an espresso and a little guilt toward Mika (17.2-35); noting a pancake recommendation on his phone (13.45-49); burning his tongue on takoyaki and joining the laughter (13.37-72); eating monaka with attention to heat and shape (9.161-189). Not B: his life outside the café and the feature is not shown. Not D: several distinct habits are located.

Directed differences: Mika (boyish reassurance at his smile, stopping at his limit, a later argument about conspicuousness, 9.161-189, 13.13-49, 19.49-78); Mizuki (attraction, shame at his assumption, the sting of being sized up, 9.34-93); Chisato (her enthusiasm reshapes his pitch, and he interprets her lending, 9.120-147, 15.63-79); Kurumi (the question he cannot answer, 17.2-35); Itō (comparing observations about Kana, 18.32-64); the photographer as a professional acquaintance (22.2-56); the regulars as a delighted first audience (19.28-70). Not B: most relationships are sampled in one or two scenes, and he has no knowledge of the café's operational life. Not D: the differences are located with what produces them.

The narration stays close to him: his hunger for recognition (9.2-23, 9.113-125), shame about emancipation (9.73-93), recognizing the film hunter in himself (15.63-79), guilt over the sugar (17.2-35), relief and the look back at the spoon (17.73-91), pride and hurt at the delivery and the self-correction about discovery (19.28-78). Not A: one book, and what he actually suspects about the café stays open (9.137-149). Not C: his reasoning is located at each turn.

Located: accepting Mika's refusal while privately regretting it (9.120-189); objecting to the setting Mizuki proposes for a confession to Mika (9.113-119); pointing out to Mika that the girls might have had a smaller part had the shop let him feature it (19.49-65); covering embarrassment with a question after his pose is corrected (15.30-56). Not C: the conflicts are mild and none is sustained; a direct objection from a photographed subject is untested. Not E: several located disagreements.

The row does not claim ethics. Located: shame at having treated his idea of emancipation as Mizuki's (9.73-93); his belief that adults know where to stop, met when Mika turns aside (13.13-23); hearing the shutter after he declared the shoot over and going straight to the picture's chances, with no question about permission shown (22.33-56). Not C: no weighing of competing obligations is rendered. Not E: the portrait analyzes the permission question his conduct leaves open.

Located only: laughing at himself after burning his tongue on takoyaki (13.37-72) and his amusement at the cigar-shaped monaka (9.161-189). Not D: two brief instances; most of the comedy around him is the narrator's.

The portrait covers his appearances across Ordinary days with spine-and-paragraph locators and keeps others' readings attributed: Mizuki's joke, the photographer's speculation, Takina's explanation of the pose, the unlabelled voices at the delivery; it marks his speculations as his. Not A: one derived item, and speech and ethics are not claimed. Not C: his located appearances are covered and attributed.

Located bounds against overreading: no courtship with Mizuki and no account of his divorce (9.34-93); his explanations of the girls' skill and of Mika's childhood are not facts (15.63-105); Itō, not he, made the reference photographs (15.96-105); he is not Kana's confidant and writes no story about her (18.32-64, 18.829-875); the issue does not show the participants asked about the extra exposure, and neither girl complains (22.2-56, 19.28-69); the wish to be first has dwindled, not disappeared (19.49-78); the newcomer at the closing bell is unidentified (19.69-78); the Recovery days photographs and message are not his (Recovery days 10.242-265, 12.443-474). Not A: no forecast is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

Located: his age (twenty-eight), the usual since about the previous week (9.12-37), the deadline the night before (17.2-35), and the order of his visits, with the bonus shoot printed after the afterword but occurring before the delivery (22.2-56, 19.7-49). Not B: no calendar dates, and the issue is not dated against the TV series. Not D: the order and several intervals are located.

scenario_readiness.note: The row does not claim speech and the portrait does not analyze his register; only reported speech acts are located.

conditions: A host or source turns a personal question aside with a smile or a change of subject: predict that he recognizes the limit, stops, and takes up what is offered instead (13.13-23, 13.45-49).
A refusal of coverage from a place he likes: predict that he accepts it, regrets it privately and keeps coming as a regular (9.120-189).
People around him show unusual composure or skill: predict that he builds an explanation from what he sees and keeps some doubt; his explanations are not facts about them (15.30-105, 22.2-32).

A photograph or feature he has worked on: predict that he judges its chances with editors and its effect on his copy's readership, takes pleasure in others' delight and feels the slight when his text is passed over (22.33-56, 19.28-70).

Include his mistakes: overconfidence in his own competence (15.30-56); treating his own idea as someone else's wish (9.73-93); assuming a precaution will protect him (13.37-72); offering a benign explanation of a child's circumstances (18.32-64).

Exclude: what he would do with a revealing anecdote or with the café's secret; a direct objection to publication from a photographed person, or editorial pressure; the café's operational life; romance; his later career; and anything that needs a performed voice.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Ordinary days from the pitch (S9) to the delivery of the issue (S19), with the bonus shoot (S22) before the delivery; split at 19.49-78, after which the café's being special to him outweighs, without erasing, the wish to introduce it.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Mika, Mizuki, Chisato, Takina, Kurumi and the regulars Itō, Doi and Yoneoka as café company; the photographer as a professional acquaintance; Kana only as someone observed. A comparable new proprietor, source or editor is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: Café LycoReco, Kinshichō and the feature's location shoot.
No television identity, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation from located acts and the portrait's closing section. What he does with sensitive knowledge and with an objection to publication is excluded.

conditions: Café counter settings with staff and regulars: his usual seat and order, laptop work, attention to food, and joining laughter after embarrassment (9.12-37, 13.37-72, 17.2-35, 19.28-70).
Excluded: his life outside the café and the feature, and any romance.
scenario_readiness.note: His café company is located; his life outside it is not.
The row does not claim ethics; the one located permission question, the extra exposure, is not raised by him, and his response to an objection is untested (22.33-56).
His attraction to Mizuki is noted with no courtship, his divorce is unexplained, and no romance is analyzed (9.34-93).

conditions: Freelance feature work: pitching a place he likes and accepting a refusal while remaining a regular (9.95-189); interview questions stopped by a source's deflection, with recommendations noted (13.2-49); a location shoot and judging a photograph's chances with editors (22.2-56); pride in delivery and the slight when his copy is passed over (19.28-70).
Excluded: negotiation with editors, a subject's objection to publication, investigative use of sensitive knowledge, and his later career.
scenario_readiness.note: His feature work is located from pitch to printed issue; disputes over publication are not.

known_limits.statement: The issue confirms the feeding photograph was printed but does not show the participants asked about that separate exposure; Tokuda goes straight to its chances, and neither girl complains (22.2-56, 19.28-69).
His explanations of the girls' skill and Mika's childhood are his speculation, and he keeps some doubt about them (15.63-105).
He notices the room react to the word work and dismisses the idea of a secret; what he actually suspects stays open (9.62-112, 9.137-149).
His wish to be the one who introduces the café has dwindled but not disappeared, and he keeps a little pleasure in a discovery for himself (19.49-78).
Seeing Kana's arrested spoon does not make him her confidant; he offers a benign explanation of her journeys and is party to none of her later circumstances (17.73-91, 18.32-64, 18.829-875).
His divorce is unexplained and there is no courtship with Mizuki (9.34-93).
Untested: what he would do with a revealing anecdote about a regular, a direct objection from a photographed person, or editorial pressure to publish.
Speech is not claimed on the row and the portrait does not analyze his register.
